source_papers.identity_scope: Review article reporting the authors’ earlier language-mapping studies: 5 healthy older adults, 16 aphasic/14 healthy semantic participants, 16 healthy phonological participants, and an illustrative single chronic stroke case. Cohorts distinguished; review summaries are not independent replications or evidence of causal recovery.

43 chronic stroke patients, at least 12 months post-stroke; behavioural PCA/reading correlations and continuous-tissue VBCM maps. Source pp. 3, 6, 8–14 inspected, including shared core versus pair-specific maps. Main mapping did not adjust for lesion volume.

42 adults with single left-hemisphere ischemic stroke and aphasia; observational cross-sectional outcomes at 3–157 months, MRI at 1–4 weeks. Source pp. 2–4 inspected; WAB object naming and category fluency remain distinct. No randomized treatment comparison.

32 chronic left-stroke survivors with aphasia, 30 healthy controls and supplementary comparison with 10 non-aphasic stroke survivors. Source pp. 3, 5–6, 8–9 inspected; SVR-LSM lesion burden, VBM regional volumes, and cluster-specific group contrasts distinguished. Hierarchical volume models refer to outcomes with identified clusters, not a positive auditory-comprehension volume finding.

40 chronic left-stroke survivors with history of aphasia; reference tract templates reconstructed in 27 healthy older adults. Source pp. 2–4 inspected. Direct lesion-burden associations distinguished from DTI integrity associations; sentence scores adjusted for word comprehension. Retired baseline drafts were not restored.
